name: From modules to durable architecture
summary: Explore the canonical repository model, its local readers, and the history behind each accepted change.

beats.title: One model, several readers
beats.narrative: The CLI, server, and browser use one canonical architecture model. The files describe modules and relationships. Each reader chooses what to show without copying that meaning.

beats.title: Open a module
beats.narrative: Opening a module changes the scope. Selection, focus, filters, and diagram grammar remain presentation choices. The local reader draws the selected architecture and keeps interaction responsive.

beats.title: Propose a change
beats.narrative: The shared runtime keeps stable identities across modules and flows. A proposal stores changed fields against an exact baseline. It does not copy the whole system into another board.

beats.title: Make the edit durable
beats.narrative: The runtime validates the complete intent and signs its checkpoint before changing current files. A journal coordinates installation and recovery. Readers hear the result only after durable completion.

beats.title: Draw the chosen reading
beats.narrative: The shared renderer measures text, lays out modules, and routes connections. The browser owns interaction. Exported pictures carry an exact recipe for the same reading.

beats.title: Explain what the reader selected
beats.narrative: The local workbench captures the exact pane reading for agent explanations and voice. Selection and focus travel with the model revision. Later navigation does not silently change that captured question.

beats.title: Keep and share exact history
beats.narrative: Adoption and shelving keep their decisions in retained history. Exact checkpoints preserve the inputs they explain. Sharing source files and publishing the architecture archive are separate actions.
